assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin biology led to GLP-1 receptor agonists that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with documented cardiovascular and weight benefits. It combines hormone physiology, peptide chemistry and a drug class with very large clinical reach.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide biology and therapeutic development) and Mojsov (peptide identification and characterization) form a plausible three-person set; Knudsen's industrial drug-development role is important but the three-laureate limit forces a choice. Contributions of others in early proglucagon work are not in the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism and clinical efficacy have been confirmed repeatedly in large independent trials over more than a decade; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among academic discoverers and the industrial developer is contested.
Recent long-term safety questions are not fully resolved from my knowledge, though they do not undermine the core discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and has reshaped circuit analysis, including work on motor and sensory circuits. The method is original, broadly adopted and clearly a tool-defining discovery.
assessment.attribution: Credit spans microbial opsin discovery and channel characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg), the neuronal demonstration (Boyden, Deisseroth) and earlier genetic photoactivation (Miesenböck). A fair three-person set is difficult; I propose Deisseroth for neuronal implementation, with Nagel and Hegemann for the channelrhodopsin discovery, and acknowledge that Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and used across thousands of laboratories for 15 or more years; timing is mature.
uncertainties: Six credited people exceed the three-laureate limit, so any configuration omits strong contributors.
Clinical translation (e.g. vision restoration) is still early, though this is not required for recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living therapeutics, with multiple approved products.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation with CD19 CAR-T, 4-1BB costimulation) and Sadelain (CD28 costimulation, preclinical foundations) are the strongest pair; Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials are significant but his contribution is partly adjacent. The original CAR concept by Eshhar is not in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Strong clinical confirmation across several indications; limits in solid tumors and toxicity remain but do not undermine the core finding.
uncertainties: Omission of the original CAR concept (not in the supplied credit) complicates a fair configuration.
Durability and long-term safety data continue to accumulate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of BCL11A as a repressor of fetal hemoglobin explained hemoglobin switching and led to the first CRISPR-based therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia, a clean path from human genetics to cure.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran established BCL11A's role; Bauer developed the enhancer-targeting strategy that underpinned editing therapy. Thein's genetic-association work on HbF is relevant but more peripheral. The three-person set is reasonably coherent, though it may overlap with CRISPR-related recognition already given.
assessment.maturity: A therapy was approved in 2023 and patient follow-up is relatively short; mechanism is well confirmed, but long-term outcomes are still maturing, so the case may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Relation to the prior CRISPR prize may affect committee appetite.
Long-term clinical durability is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, which changed the natural history of spinal muscular atrophy, a motor neuron disease of direct interest from a motor-system viewpoint. It is a rigorous mechanism-to-drug story in RNA therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are a natural pair; contributions of the Hua/Singh and clinical teams are not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with years of real-world data; confirmation is strong and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Mechanism-level credit among several groups, including others not listed, is not fully clear.
Whether the committee views this as a platform or single-disease advance is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of cGAS-STING connected cytosolic DNA sensing to innate immunity, autoimmunity and anti-tumor responses, a conceptual advance in innate signaling.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger; Barber identified STING. This pairing captures the two decisive steps; Ishikawa's early STING work is also relevant but the other listed names are less central.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed but therapeutic translation is limited so far, making the case somewhat early compared with drug-validated candidates.
uncertainties: Clinical impact in cancer and autoimmunity is still unproven.
Credit around STING discovery (several groups in 2008-2009) is partly contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established molecularly targeted therapy and transformed CML into a chronic, manageable disease, a paradigm shift for oncology.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (compound discovery) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) is a coherent trio. Roles of Rowley and Nowell/Hungerford (Philadelphia chromosome), and of Ben Hunter-type chemistry teams, are outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with long-term survival data, but significant prior recognition (Lasker, etc.) and the possibility that it should have been honored earlier exist.
uncertainties: Whether the prize committee finds the discovery sufficiently distinct from the earlier oncogene and Philadelphia chromosome work.
Resistance biology credit may fall to Sawyers or others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus offers dramatic symptomatic relief in Parkinson's disease and has opened neuromodulation approaches. It is clinically impactful and relevant to motor-circuit physiology.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the single person credited; DeLong's basal ganglia circuit model and Benazzouz's STN lesion work are also central, but only the supplied name can be proposed.
assessment.maturity: Widely used for decades with extensive independent confirmation, though the underlying mechanism of action remains debated.
uncertainties: The mechanism of DBS benefit is not settled.
Credit shared with basal ganglia circuit researchers and others not in the supplied credit may complicate a single-laureate configuration.
